$comment: Accepted exceptions for the map-audit skill (.claude/skills/map-audit). A decision with verdict 'accepted' suppresses matching findings on every future run, so a deliberate choice never gets re-litigated. Written ONLY on an explicit human call — never by an agent acting on its own judgement.

$schema_notes.rule: the rule code being excepted, e.g. 'SCAV-1'. See rules.md.
$schema_notes.scope: which tiles the exception covers. Every key present must match. An empty scope {} excepts the whole rule world-wide — use sparingly. Keys: zone_id, terrain, region_id, district, name, map_id (each accepts a string or an array), and name_pattern (a case-insensitive regex).
$schema_notes.verdict: 'accepted' suppresses the finding. 'todo' records the decision without suppressing, for things deferred rather than accepted.
$schema_notes.decided_by: who made the call — a real person. 'John' or 'Dave'.
$schema_notes.reason: why. Written for the person who finds this in a year and wonders.

decisions.reason: Genuinely always-open thresholds, reviewed building by building. Architect Shrine opens on a nave and is open to the faithful; The Ascension Gate's interior IS the checkpoint (The Scanline), so a door in front of it would be a redundant second threshold; KSAB Audience Gate is the public audience entrance to a broadcast lobby. The other 38 doorless buildings all got doors in the same pass.

The Echelon is the one legitimately dynamic entrance in the world: plugins/yacht/index.js sets flags.entrance from whichever pier she ties up against and deletes it while she is underway. A hardcoded cardinal interior link would contradict her the moment she docks on a different side, so 'in' is correct here and must stay.
